one_liner: Branchless, expression-only HSV-to-RGB float function in a public-domain C header, about 5.7x faster than the textbook 6-way switch on random input.
what_it_does: A tiny benchmark repo whose reusable part is hsv.h: fast_hsv_to_rgb(h, s, v, float* rgb) converts one HSV triple (all components in [0,1]) to float RGB with the same signature as the classic switch-based hsv_to_rgb in the same header. The header also carries the switch version, an implied-value hs_to_rgb, hsl_to_rgb and scalar sRGB/linear transfer functions. hsvbench.c times the switch, the branchless expression and a 17x17 bilinear lookup table over 1M random pixels, 300 passes each.
how_it_is_fast: Each channel is a piecewise-linear 'tent' of the hue: r = |6h-3|-1, g = 2-|6h-2|, b = 2-|6h-4|, each clamped to [0,1] and blended with saturation and value, so there is no sector index, no floor() and no switch. fabsf and the ternary clamp compile to andps and min/max instructions, so the loop body is straight-line float code with no data-dependent branches and is a candidate for compiler auto-vectorisation (not confirmed by disassembly in the repo). The baseline it beats branches six ways on the hue sector and calls double-precision floor() per pixel, which at -O2 without -march (no SSE4.1 round instruction on baseline x86-64) is typically a libm call (inference from the Makefile flags, not measured).
when_to_use: Per-pixel or per-vertex HSV-to-RGB in C or C++ code (colour pickers, procedural palettes, particle and heat-map colouring) where pulling in OpenCV or a colour library is overkill.
Hot loops over float HSV data whose hues vary unpredictably from one element to the next, where the switch version mispredicts most.
Code you want to auto-vectorise or port to SIMD intrinsics or shaders: the function is branch-free and uses only abs, min/max, multiply and add.
Projects that need public-domain (Unlicense) code to paste in without attribution.
when_not_to_use: Whole-image 8-bit conversions: OpenCV cvtColor (COLOR_HSV2RGB) or a SIMD colour converter works on packed u8 buffers and threads; hsvbench never compares against any library.

When you need bit-identical output with an existing switch implementation: 396 of 65,536 test pixels differ by 1 LSB in 8-bit (README ppmhist), partly because the bundled switch version scales hue by 5.9999 rather than 6.
Hue values outside [0,1] or in degrees: the expression does not wrap (h = 1.2 clamps to pure red instead of hue 0.2), so wrap and normalise before calling.
Spatially coherent real images, where the switch's branches predict well; the 5.7x was measured on uniformly random hues, the worst case for the baseline, so expect a smaller gain.
Anyone wanting a maintained library: 7 commits on one day (2020-12-08), no tests, no issues or releases.

integration.dependencies: libm (<math.h> must be included before hsv.h; the header uses fabsf, floor and powf without including it)
integration.min_toolchain: C99 with the GNU __inline__ keyword (GCC or Clang); the Makefile uses clang-10 -std=c99 -O2. MSVC needs a #define for __inline__ (not documented).
integration.platforms: any (portable scalar float code; no intrinsics)
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; the header functions are pure and stateless, so they are reentrant (from reading hsv.h).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same signature as the header's switch-based hsv_to_rgb(h, s, v, rgb), but outputs differ by up to 1 LSB in 8-bit and there is no image-level or integer API

gotchas: CLAMP01 is an unprefixed function-like macro that evaluates its argument up to three times and does not parenthesise the second use of x; it can collide with or misbehave beside other macros.
hsv.h is not self-contained: include <math.h> first, and it defines generic names (hsv_to_rgb, hsl_to_rgb, linear_to_srgb) that may clash with other colour code.

The benchmark times whole processes with time(1), including identical setup (3M rand() calls and table init) in each run; the fast run moves about 7.5 GB of array traffic in 0.655 s (about 11.5 GB/s, derived from page data), so it may be near single-core memory bandwidth and the compute-only ratio is not isolated.

Building hsvbench.c at -O0 is likely to fail to link: hue_sat_val_lookup is a non-static C99 inline definition with no external definition; the -O2 Makefile build inlines it. The table benchmark also maps byte hue to h/256 while the reference uses h/255, so part of the table's visible error is a mapping mismatch.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this over OpenCV, CompV or DeltaCV when you need a single-pixel float HSV-to-RGB function to paste into C code rather than an image-wide cvtColor call; like fast-srgb8 it is a scalar per-value transform measured only against a naive reference, so for bulk 8-bit image conversion the library siblings remain the better-evidenced choice.
verified_claims_summary: On the author's unnamed CPU, with clang-10 -O2 (no -march), 300 passes over 1,048,576 random float HSV pixels took 3.745 s for the switch formula, 0.655 s for the branchless expression and 1.865 s for the lookup table, measured as whole-process wall time (about 5.7x and 2.0x, derived from page data). The baseline is the repo's own textbook switch, not a library, and no CPU model or repeat count is given.
status_note: Abandoned since 2020-12-08 (all 7 commits on one day, no issues or PRs), but Unlicense and only a 20-line function, so it is trivial to vendor.
